item.stem: The daily amount of time teenagers spend on a specific social media app is heavily right-skewed, as shown in the population distribution [FIGURE:fig1]. The population mean is $\mu = 4.5$ hours and the population standard deviation is $\sigma = 2.2$ hours. A researcher plans to take many random samples of size $n$ from this population and calculate the sample mean $\bar{x}$ for each sample to build a sampling distribution of the mean. Which of the following is true regarding the resulting sampling distribution?

options.text: For a sample size of $n = 100$, the sampling distribution of $\bar{x}$ will be approximately normal with a mean of $4.5$ hours.
options.rationale: The student correctly understands that for a sufficiently large sample ($n=100$), the Central Limit Theorem ensures the sampling distribution is approximately normal (A2) and that its mean remains equal to the population mean (A3).

options.text: The sampling distribution of $\bar{x}$ will be approximately normal with a mean of $4.5$ hours, regardless of whether the sample size is $n = 2$ or $n = 100$.
options.rationale: The student correctly identifies the mean (A3) but incorrectly believes that the sampling distribution of the mean is always normal, regardless of the sample size or the skewness of the underlying population (B12).

options.text: For a sample size of $n = 100$, the sampling distribution of $\bar{x}$ will be approximately normal with a mean of $4.5 / \sqrt{100} = 0.45$ hours.
options.rationale: The student correctly identifies that the distribution becomes normal for large $n$ (A2) but incorrectly believes that the mean of the sampling distribution decreases as sample size increases, confusing the mean with the standard error formula (B13).

options.text: For a sample size of $n = 100$, the sampling distribution of $\bar{x}$ will be heavily right-skewed with a mean of $4.5$ hours.
options.rationale: The student correctly identifies the mean (A3) but fails to recognize that the Central Limit Theorem causes the sampling distribution of the mean to become approximately normal as the sample size increases (A2).

item.explanation: This item tests the application of the Central Limit Theorem to the sampling distribution of the mean. Key concepts include: 1) the mean of the sampling distribution is always equal to the population mean regardless of sample size (A3); 2) for large sample sizes, the sampling distribution becomes approximately normal even if the population is skewed (A2). Distractors target the misconception that the distribution is always normal regardless of sample size (B12) or that the mean of the sampling distribution changes with sample size (B13).
